Below the text: a centred side note line "Ad inducendam appetentiam quae conueniant cibaria." set as a marginal-style note under the text, then a chapter heading "CAPVT XXIX." and the opening paragraph with a large initial. Faint show-through of the facing page is present in the left margin and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: potentia. Magis praeterea penetrat in corporis interiora ratione qualitatis igneae. Vnde ab huiusmodi aquis magis pati natiuum calorem, quàm à naturali manifestum est. Qua propter in causa frigida & ijs qui alicuius interiorum viscerum imbecillitatem patiuntur, vitandas esse destillationum aquas opinamur.

Sed non praetermittendum est sitim quandoque à ventriculo, quandoque ab iocinere & pulmone & renibus euenire posse, vt à Galeno in libris de locis affectis scriptum est. Quae à pulmone ortum habet, aqua hordei cum syrupo violarum sedat. Ab hepate aqua destillata frigida. A ventriculo, potus aqua frigida. A renibus, aqua decoctionis liquiritiae compescit.
Ad inducendam appetentiam quae conueniant cibaria.
main_text.head: CAPVT XXIX.
main_text.p: PAtiuntur febricitantes aliquando deiectionem appetentiae vt eorum corpora arescant atrophia. Cunque multiplices habeat causas

page.notes: The facing page shows through faintly in the margins; not transcribed. The word "causas" at the line end is set at the right margin. The initial P is a large woodcut letter joined to "Patiuntur" as "PAtiuntur". The lower paragraph is set in the printed form and may contain minor transcription uncertainty in the Greek-style ligatures.
